archetype: Archetype 5 (Jewel & Luxury) infused with Archetype 1 (Organic & Earthy)

headings.strategy: Use tight letter spacing (tracking-tight) for large headers. Do NOT use Inter or generic sans-serif for headings.

body.strategy: Clean, legible geometric sans for data, tools, and long-form text. Highly legible at small sizes.

mono.strategy: Use for financial numbers, tickers, and calculator inputs.

layout_and_spacing.grid_strategy: Use Bento 'Tetris' grid (asymmetric) for marketing sections. Use 'Control Room' dense grid for calculators and tools.
layout_and_spacing.border_radius: rounded-2xl for large containers, rounded-xl for cards, rounded-lg for buttons.

components.buttons: Flat solid background for primary CTAs. Always include focus-visible rings and hover states (translate-y-[-1px]). No pill shapes, use rounded-lg.
components.cards: Subtle 1px border with no default shadow. On hover: shadow-xl and -translate-y-1. Do not overuse cards; try flat bento styles.
components.glassmorphism: Strictly for sticky headers and floating tooltips. Requires backdrop-blur-xl and a delicate 1px inner stroke (border-white/20 or border-black/5).

sections_architecture.name: Hero
sections_architecture.description: Premium positioning. Large Playfair Display heading communicating 'Financial + Career Platform'. Background uses subtle abstract grain. Features an interactive dashboard/calculator preview.

sections_architecture.name: Start Here
sections_architecture.description: Clickable questions driving users to tools. Clean, asymmetric list layout.

sections_architecture.name: What You Can Do
sections_architecture.description: 4-pillar section. Bento grid layout with generous padding.

sections_architecture.name: Popular Tools
sections_architecture.description: Highlighting top tools with 'The Tracing Beam' border effect on the featured tool.

sections_architecture.name: Career Tools
sections_architecture.description: Hero-like section with dark slate background (#020617). Uses the office image with a bg-black/50 overlay. High contrast white serif text.

sections_architecture.name: What-If Simulator
sections_architecture.description: Interactive Recharts line chart showing compound growth. Minimalist card styling.

sections_architecture.name: Financial Calculators
sections_architecture.description: Dense grid of calculator links/cards. Functional UI.

sections_architecture.name: Productive Tools
sections_architecture.description: Dense grid, similar to calculators but distinct icon styling.

sections_architecture.name: Articles & Guides
sections_architecture.description: Editorial layout. Large images, serif titles, ample negative space.

sections_architecture.name: Trust
sections_architecture.description: Partner logos using Marquee strategy (Editorial Ribbon) - slow drift, low contrast.

sections_architecture.name: Email CTA
sections_architecture.description: Dark container in Jewel tone teal (#042f2e). High contrast input field.

sections_architecture.name: Footer
sections_architecture.description: Massive py-32 spacing. Brand logo prominent. Clean columns.

testing.strategy: All interactive elements, forms, and key sections must include 'data-testid' attributes (e.g., 'hero-cta-button', 'what-if-chart').

instructions_to_main_agent: Strictly follow the Old Money Tech typography pairing (Playfair Display for headings, Manrope for body). Do NOT use Inter.
Implement the 12 sections in the exact order specified in the problem statement.
Career Tools section MUST use the dark theme (#020617 background) to stand out, with the provided 'career_office' image with an overlay.
Use Recharts for the 'What-If' simulator chart. Ensure it looks premium (no default axes styling, use monospace font for numbers, custom tooltip).
Replace generic card styles with 1px borders and subtle hover lifts. No heavy drop shadows.
Do NOT use transparent headers over images without a backdrop-blur glassmorphism effect.
Ensure the hero section communicates the financial + career dual-purpose within 5 seconds through clear H1 and layout.
Write code for React (.jsx/.js files), not TypeScript (.tsx) as specified in the strict instructions.
